group.text: Security and Privacy Analysis through Risk-driven Threat Assessment

SPARTA automatically elicits threats from a Data Flow Diagram (DFD) model of your system and prioritizes them by risk. Follow the guided tutorial, start from a bundled example, or create your own project.

group.label: Getting started
group.text: 1. Create a modeling project and a SPARTA model (DFD Model) for your system.
2. Draw the system's data flow diagram in the graphical DFD editor.
3. Attach a threat catalog (e.g. STRIDE or LINDDUN) to the model.
4. Analyze it in the Threat Analysis view to elicit and prioritize threats.
5. Apply security solutions and refine the model as your design evolves.

group.label: What's new in the 2026 release line

group.text: Welcome screen, examples and tutorial
This page, bundled example projects, and a step-by-step tutorial that runs inside the workbench.
SPARTA menu and toolbar
Analyze, clear and export from the main menu and toolbar, even when the Threat Analysis view is closed.
Diagram improvements
Improved views and editing, a Loss Estimates layer, and table editors for threat type catalogs and attacker profiles.
VQL pattern editor
Edit threat patterns with syntax highlighting (right-click > Edit VQL Pattern...). The Pattern Support view in the SPARTA perspective reports pattern problems.
Reports with DFD diagrams
Threat reports now include the model's data flow diagrams, drawn in TikZ from their diagram layout. Reports can also be exported from the command line.
Richer threat exports
CSV and XLSX exports add trust boundary crossings, nesting depth, parent elements and trust boundaries, and involved solutions.
Multi-line properties
Edit descriptions, conditions and patterns as multi-line text in the Properties view.
Releases for every platform on GitHub
Each release is published on GitHub with Windows, macOS and Linux products, an Eclipse update site per release line (/updates/2026/), and Maven artifacts for the standalone libraries.
More reliable analysis
Fixes for legacy interaction-based threat patterns and for estimates whose minimum equals their maximum. Risk calculation failures are now logged, and Threat Analysis sorting is more stable.
Sturdier CLI and CI tools

Non-zero exit codes on failure, UTF-8 output for all exporters, and timeouts on server submission. Catalogs with missing values export correctly, and failed report exports are reported instead of producing partial output.
CLI option change
Ambiguous two-letter CLI option shortcodes were removed. Check scripts that use them.
Roles bound to multiple elements
A solution's role binding can now bind to any number of DFD elements, so one solution can cover several flows or processes.
Open source
SPARTA is now open source under the Eclipse Public License 2.0, developed on GitHub alongside its example cases and threat catalogs.
Threat report export
Export a LaTeX threat report from the Threat Analysis view, generated from templates with a Tufte-book layout and TikZ data flow diagram styles.
Risk from data type estimates
Risk calculation now includes estimates defined on data types, and the data types diagram was updated to match.
Custom threat patterns in the CLI
The CLI handles custom threat patterns, with number formatting for pattern-based threats.
Conditional diagram styling
Diagram editor layers support conditional styling.
Complete threat descriptions
Exported threat descriptions now have their parameters filled in.
VQL: threatened is now location
Threat patterns use location instead of threatened in the VQL queries too. Models that still use threatened keep working.
Eclipse 2025-06 and Java 21
The platform moved to Eclipse 2025-06 on Java 21, with Guice upgraded and javax.inject replaced by jakarta.inject.
Fixes
A crash in the CSV export, threats and threat types being mixed up in the Threat Analysis view, and engine resource set handling (also used by the CLI).

group.label: About & support
group.text: SPARTA is developed by DistriNet (KU Leuven) and released under the Eclipse Public License v2.0. This is the 2026 release line. To report an issue or request support, use the contact and issue-tracker links on the SPARTA website.

group.text: Create and analyze your first model

You model a small web shop, let SPARTA elicit and prioritize its threats, and mitigate them with a security solution. The tutorial opens as a panel beside the workbench. Each step explains what to do, and many can be carried out for you with a single click.

group.label: What you will do
group.text: 1. Open the SPARTA perspective and create the tutorial project. It comes with a STRIDE threat catalog and a security solution catalog.
2. Create a DFD model and its data flow diagram.
3. Draw a trust boundary, processes, a data store, an external entity and the data flows between them.
4. Attach the threat catalog and analyze the model in the Threat Analysis view.
5. Optionally, add loss estimates so the risk ranking reflects your system.
6. Apply a SecurePipe solution and watch the risk of the mitigated threats drop.
7. Export the results as a threat report or spreadsheet.
